subject: Art & Design
title: Cognitive Load: Don't Overwhelm the Brain
description: A quick win: understand Cognitive Load: Don't Overwhelm the Brain.

hook.text: You open a website and see 50 buttons, 3 pop-ups, and flashing banners. Your brain says: leave. Immediately.

buildup.text: Cognitive load is the total mental effort required to use a product. High load = frustration and errors.

discovery.text: Working memory holds about 4 items at once. Exceed that, and users start forgetting, making mistakes, and quitting.

twist.text: Simplicity isn't about fewer features. It's about progressive disclosure: reveal complexity only when users need it.

climax.text: Google's homepage is one search bar. Yet Google is the most complex product in the world. Complexity is hidden.

punchline.text: Great design doesn't make users think less. It makes thinking effortless.

quiz.question: What is 'progressive disclosure' in design?
options: Revealing complexity gradually, only when users need it
Showing all features at once for transparency
Slowly loading content to improve performance

details.summary: Cognitive load measures the mental effort required to process information. Overloaded interfaces — too many options, dense text, competing visuals — exhaust working memory and cause users to abandon tasks.
details.whyItMatters: Working memory is severely limited — humans can hold roughly four items simultaneously. Every unnecessary element in a design competes for that scarce resource. Reducing cognitive load is the most direct path to usable, effective interfaces.
takeaways: Cognitive load measures mental effort to process information
Humans can hold roughly four items in working memory
Reducing clutter and choices minimizes cognitive load

faq.question: What are the three types of cognitive load?
faq.answer: Intrinsic load is the inherent complexity of the task itself. Extraneous load is unnecessary complexity added by poor design — confusing navigation, irrelevant decorations, unclear labels. Germane load is productive effort that builds understanding. Good design minimizes extraneous load.

faq.question: How does chunking reduce cognitive load?
faq.answer: Chunking groups related information into meaningful units. A phone number as 555-123-4567 (three chunks) is easier to remember than 5551234567 (ten digits). In design, chunking means organizing content into logical sections with clear headings, whitespace, and visual grouping.
